025/**
026 * The configuration of a RainbowGum. In some other logging implementations this is called
027 * "context".
028 */
029public sealed interface LogConfig extends LogProperty.PropertySupport {
030
031        /**
032         * String key value properties.
033         * @return properties.
034         */
035        @Override
036        public LogProperties properties();
037
038        /**
039         * Level resolver for resolving levels from logger names.
040         * @return level resolver.
041         */
042        public LevelConfig levelResolver();
043
044        /**
045         * Output provider that uses URI to find output.
046         * @return output provider.
047         */
048        public LogOutputRegistry outputRegistry();
049
050        /**
051         * Provides encoders by URI scheme.
052         * @return encoder registry.
053         */
054        public LogEncoderRegistry encoderRegistry();
055
056        /**
057         * Provides publishers by URI scheme.
058         * @return changePublisher registry.
059         */
060        public LogPublisherRegistry publisherRegistry();
061
062        /**
063         * Creates a builder for making LogConfig.
064         * @return builder.
065         */
066        public static Builder builder() {
067                return new Builder();
068        }
069
070        /**
071         * An event changePublisher to publish configuration changes.
072         * @return changePublisher.
073         */
074        public ChangePublisher changePublisher();
075
076        /**
077         * Service registry are custom services needed by plugins particularly during the
078         * initialization process.
079         * @return registry.
080         */
081        public ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry();
082
083        /**
084         * Alerts about problems with the logging system itself (as opposed to application
085         * logging routed through the {@link LogRouter}).
086         * @return alerts.
087         */
088        public LogAlerts alerts();
089
090        /**
091         * Metrics about the logging system itself (as opposed to application logging routed
092         * through the {@link LogRouter}).
093         * @return metrics.
094         */
095        public LogMetrics metrics();
096
097        /**
098         * Mixin for config support.
099         */
100        interface ConfigSupport extends LogProperty.PropertySupport {
101
102                /**
103                 * Provides config.
104                 * @return config.
105                 */
106                public LogConfig config();
107
108                @Override
109                default LogProperties properties() {
110                        return config().properties();
111                }
112
113        }
114
115        /**
116         * Config Change Publisher. By default this is enabled with
117         * {@value LogProperties#GLOBAL_CHANGE_PROPERTY} set to <code>true</code>, which then
118         * gates two independent, per-logger-name properties:
119         * {@value LogProperties#CHANGE_PREFIX} + {@value LogProperties#SEP} + logger name,
120         * set to a list of {@link ChangeType} or <code>true</code>/<code>false</code> to
121         * enable or disable all changes, and {@value LogProperties#CALLER_PREFIX} +
122         * {@value LogProperties#SEP} + logger name, set to a {@link CallerType} (or
123         * <code>true</code>/<code>false</code>) to control caller info. The two are resolved
124         * independently - one does not imply or override the other, even for overlapping
125         * logger name prefixes.
126         */
127        interface ChangePublisher {
128
129                /**
130                 * Subscribe to changes.
131                 * @param consumer consumer.
132                 */
133                public void subscribe(Consumer<? super LogConfig> consumer);
134
135                /**
136                 * Publish that there has been changes.
137                 */
138                public void publish();
139
140                /**
141                 * Test to see if <strong>any</strong> changes are enabled for a logger - either
142                 * {@link #allowedChanges(String)} is non-empty or {@link #callerType(String)} is
143                 * not {@link CallerType#NONE}.
144                 * @param loggerName logger name.
145                 * @return true if enabled.
146                 */
147                public boolean isEnabled(String loggerName);
148
149                /**
150                 * Returns what the logger is allowed to change.
151                 * @param loggerName logger name.
152                 * @return which things are allowed to change in the logger
153                 */
154                public Set<ChangeType> allowedChanges(String loggerName);
155
156                /**
157                 * The caller info strategy for a logger, resolved from
158                 * {@value LogProperties#CALLER_PREFIX}, independently of
159                 * {@link #allowedChanges(String)} /{@value LogProperties#CHANGE_PREFIX}. Unlike
160                 * {@link ChangeType#LEVEL}, which is genuinely re-evaluated on every
161                 * {@link #publish()}, this is resolved once when a logger is first created and
162                 * never revisited afterward - it reflects a static per-logger capability, not
163                 * something that changes at runtime.
164                 * @param loggerName logger name.
165                 * @return caller type, {@link CallerType#NONE} if not configured.
166                 */
167                public CallerType callerType(String loggerName);
168
169                /**
170                 * Whether caller info should be computed for a logger at all, regardless of which
171                 * non-{@link CallerType#NONE} strategy.
172                 * @param loggerName logger name.
173                 * @return true if caller info is enabled for this logger.
174                 */
175                default boolean callerInfoEnabled(String loggerName) {
176                        return callerType(loggerName) != CallerType.NONE;
177                }
178
179                /**
180                 * Changing type options.
181                 */
182                public enum ChangeType {
183
184                        /**
185                         * No changes are allowed. Synonymous with <code>false</code> - never actually
186                         * present in a {@link #allowedChanges(String)} result (that case is just the
187                         * empty set); this exists so a single malformed-vs-explicitly-off token can
188                         * be told apart while parsing, and so <code>false</code> is a real,
189                         * documented enum member rather than only a magic string.
190                         */
191                        NONE,
192                        /**
193                         * The logger is allowed to change levels.
194                         */
195                        LEVEL;
196
197                        static Set<ChangeType> parse(List<String> value) {
198                                if (value.isEmpty()) {
199                                        return Set.of();
200                                }
201                                var s = EnumSet.noneOf(ChangeType.class);
202                                for (var v : value) {
203                                        if (v.equalsIgnoreCase("true")) {
204                                                return EnumSet.complementOf(EnumSet.of(ChangeType.NONE));
205                                        }
206                                        var ct = ChangeType.parse(v);
207                                        if (ct == NONE) {
208                                                return EnumSet.noneOf(ChangeType.class);
209                                        }
210                                        s.add(ct);
211                                }
212                                return s;
213                        }
214
215                        static ChangeType parse(String value) {
216                                String v = value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
217                                return switch (v) {
218                                        case "FALSE" -> NONE;
219                                        default -> ChangeType.valueOf(v);
220                                };
221                        }
222
223                }
224
225        }
226
227        /**
228         * Builder for LogConfig.
229         * <p>
230         * <strong>NOTE:</strong> The service loader is not used by default with this builder.
231         * If the automatic discovery of components is desired call
232         * {@link #serviceLoader(ServiceLoader)}.
233         */
234        public static final class Builder extends LevelResolver.AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
235
236                private @Nullable ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry;
237
238                private @Nullable LogProperties logProperties;
239
240                private @Nullable ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> serviceLoader;
241
242                private final List<RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator> configurators = new ArrayList<>();
243
244                private final List<RainbowGumServiceProvider.PropertiesProvider> propertiesProviders = new ArrayList<>();
245
246                /**
247                 * Default constructor
248                 */
249                private Builder() {
250                }
251
252                /**
253                 * Sets log properties
254                 * @param logProperties log properties.
255                 * @return this.
256                 */
257                public Builder properties(LogProperties logProperties) {
258                        this.logProperties = logProperties;
259                        return this;
260                }
261
262                /**
263                 * Sets service registry
264                 * @param serviceRegistry service registry.
265                 * @return this.
266                 */
267                public Builder serviceRegistry(ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry) {
268                        this.serviceRegistry = serviceRegistry;
269                        return this;
270                }
271
272                /**
273                 * Add to configure LogConfig and ServiceRegistry.
274                 * @param configurator will run on build.
275                 * @return this.
276                 */
277                public Builder configurator(RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator configurator) {
278                        configurators.add(configurator);
279                        return this;
280                }
281
282                /**
283                 * Add properties.
284                 * @param propertiesProvider will run on build.
285                 * @return this.
286                 */
287                public Builder propertiesProvider(RainbowGumServiceProvider.PropertiesProvider propertiesProvider) {
288                        propertiesProviders.add(propertiesProvider);
289                        return this;
290                }
291
292                /**
293                 * Sets the service loader to use for loading components that were not set.
294                 * @param serviceLoader loader to use for missing components.
295                 * @return this.
296                 */
297                public Builder serviceLoader(ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> serviceLoader) {
298                        this.serviceLoader = serviceLoader;
299                        return this;
300                }
301
302                /**
303                 * Sets a default service loader to use for loading components that were not set.
304                 * This call will just call the {@link ServiceLoader} without providing a class
305                 * loader.
306                 * @return this.
307                 */
308                public Builder serviceLoader() {
309                        return this.serviceLoader(ServiceLoader.load(RainbowGumServiceProvider.class));
310                }
311
312                /**
313                 * Configures the builder with a function for ergonomics.
314                 * @param consumer passed the builder.
315                 * @return this.
316                 */
317                public Builder with(Consumer<? super Builder> consumer) {
318                        consumer.accept(this);
319                        return this;
320                }
321
322                /**
323                 * Builds LogConfig which will use the {@link ServiceLoader} if set to load
324                 * missing components and if not set will use static defaults.
325                 * @return log config
326                 */
327                public LogConfig build() {
328                        ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry = this.serviceRegistry;
329                        LogProperties logProperties = this.logProperties;
330
331                        var serviceLoader = this.serviceLoader;
332                        var configurators = this.configurators;
333                        if (serviceRegistry == null) {
334                                serviceRegistry = ServiceRegistry.of();
335                        }
336                        if (logProperties == null) {
337                                List<LogProperties> props = new ArrayList<>();
338                                for (var pp : propertiesProviders) {
339                                        props.addAll(pp.provideProperties(serviceRegistry));
340                                }
341                                if (props.isEmpty() && serviceLoader != null) {
342                                        props.addAll(provideProperties(serviceRegistry, serviceLoader));
343                                }
344                                logProperties = LogProperties.of(props, LogProperties.StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES);
345
346                        }
347                        /*
348                         * Built before DefaultLogConfig itself (rather than left for
349                         * DefaultLogConfig's constructor to create, as before) specifically so
350                         * buildGlobalResolver below can hand LogAlerts to the global level resolver's
351                         * alerting wrapper - the global resolver is built before a full LogConfig
352                         * exists to pull config.alerts() from, so alerts (and metrics, via alerts'
353                         * own listener wiring) are constructed directly here instead. Capacity and
354                         * logging.alerts.unobservedErrorsAction both come from logProperties as
355                         * already resolved above - before any configurator runs, the same as
356                         * everything else built directly in this method - see
357                         * DefaultLogAlerts.of(...) for how the two are validated together.
358                         */
359                        LogAlerts alerts = DefaultLogAlerts.of(logProperties);
360                        LogMetrics metrics = new DefaultLogMetrics();
361                        var levelResolver = this.buildGlobalResolver(logProperties, alerts);
362                        var config = new DefaultLogConfig(serviceRegistry, logProperties, levelResolver, alerts, metrics);
363                        if (serviceLoader != null) {
364                                configurators = new ArrayList<>(configurators);
365                                findProviders(serviceLoader, Configurator.class).forEach(configurators::add);
366                        }
367                        if (!configurators.isEmpty()) {
368                                /*
369                                 * TODO two-pass config: configurators run after config (and therefore the
370                                 * global level resolver above) already exists, so a configurator that
371                                 * contributes additional property sources or otherwise changes what the
372                                 * level resolver should have seen is invisible to it - the resolver was
373                                 * already built from logProperties as it stood before any configurator
374                                 * ran. A more correct design would run configurators first, then rebuild
375                                 * whatever is purely derived from properties (starting with the level
376                                 * resolver) a second time against the now-fully-configured LogConfig. Not
377                                 * done here - see todo.md.
378                                 */
379                                RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator.runConfigurators(configurators.stream(), config);
380                        }
381                        /*
382                         * Deliberately last: alerts already resolved LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction
383                         * at construction above, but only now, once configurators have had their
384                         * chance to record alerts and/or register a real Listener, does "should I
385                         * report/refuse to start" actually mean anything - by construction nothing
386                         * has had a chance to register one before this point.
387                         */
388                        alerts.start(config);
389                        return config;
390                }
391
392                LevelConfig buildGlobalResolver(LogProperties logProperties, LogAlerts alerts) {
393                        LevelConfig levelResolver = LevelConfig
394                                .of(List.of(ConfigLevelResolver.of(logProperties), GroupLevelResolver.of(logProperties)));
395                        var config = buildLevelConfigOrNull();
396                        if (config != null) {
397                                levelResolver = LevelConfig.of(List.<LevelConfig>of(config, levelResolver));
398                        }
399                        return new AlertingLevelConfig(levelResolver, alerts);
400                }
401
402                private static List<LogProperties> provideProperties(ServiceRegistry registry,
403                                ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> loader) {
404                        List<LogProperties> props = findProviders(loader, PropertiesProvider.class)
405                                .flatMap(s -> s.provideProperties(registry).stream())
406                                .toList();
407                        return props;
408                }
409
410                @Override
411                protected Builder self() {
412                        return this;
413                }
414
415        }
416
417}
418
419abstract class AbstractChangePublisher implements ChangePublisher {
420
421        /*
422         * TODO Ideally this would be a concurrent weak hashmap. The reasoning is we may want
423         * a configuration where SLF4J loggers are not stored in concurrent hash map but some
424         * sort of GC friendly cache or not cached at all. If they subscribe to changes the
425         * loggers will never be GCed.
426         *
427         * Consequently the functional Consumer interface might not be the best choice.
428         */
429        private final Collection<Consumer<? super LogConfig>> consumers = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<Consumer<? super LogConfig>>();
430
431        /*
432         * Same shape as LevelResolver.java's CachedLevelResolver: allowedChanges(name) is
433         * only ever called once per never-before-seen logger name (RainbowGumLoggerFactory
434         * caches the resulting Logger forever afterward), so a ConcurrentHashMap here matches
435         * the exact call pattern that made a ConcurrentHashMap the right tradeoff there too.
436         */
437        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, Set<ChangeType>> changesCache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
438
439        /*
440         * Sibling to changesCache, not folded into it - CallerType is resolved from its own
441         * logging.caller.<name> property, independent of logging.change.<name>, so it gets
442         * its own map rather than a combined per-name struct (one map per concern).
443         */
444        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, CallerType> callerTypeCache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
445
446        protected abstract LogConfig reload();
447
448        protected abstract LogConfig config();
449
450        @Override
451        public void publish() {
452                changesCache.clear();
453                callerTypeCache.clear();
454                LogConfig config = reload();
455                for (var c : consumers) {
456                        c.accept(config);
457                }
458        }
459
460        @Override
461        public void subscribe(Consumer<? super LogConfig> consumer) {
462                consumers.add(consumer);
463        }
464
465        @Override
466        public boolean isEnabled(String loggerName) {
467                return !allowedChanges(loggerName).isEmpty() || callerType(loggerName) != CallerType.NONE;
468        }
469
470        @Override
471        public Set<ChangeType> allowedChanges(String loggerName) {
472                return changesCache.computeIfAbsent(loggerName, n -> {
473                        /*
474                         * findOrNull walks the logger-name hierarchy (closest match wins, see its own
475                         * javadoc) trying each candidate key in turn - per candidate, resolve it as a
476                         * LogProperty and only return null (telling findOrNull to keep walking up)
477                         * when the key is genuinely Missing there. A present-but-malformed value is a
478                         * Result.Error, not a Missing - it must stop the walk right there rather than
479                         * silently falling through to a less specific ancestor's value.
480                         */
481                        LogProperty.Result<Set<ChangeType>> result = config().properties()
482                                .findOrNull(LogProperties.CHANGE_PREFIX, n, (props, fullKey) -> {
483                                        LogProperty.Result<Set<ChangeType>> r = props.forKey(fullKey).ofList().map(ChangeType::parse);
484                                        return r instanceof LogProperty.Result.Missing ? null : r;
485                                });
486                        if (result == null) {
487                                return Set.of();
488                        }
489                        try {
490                                return result.validateNow(ChangePublisher.class);
491                        }
492                        catch (LogProperty.ValidationException e) {
493                                /*
494                                 * A malformed logging.change.<name> value must not be able to break
495                                 * logging itself. ConcurrentHashMap#computeIfAbsent leaves nothing cached
496                                 * when the mapping function throws, so without catching this a bad
497                                 * property would re-parse and re-alert on every single allowedChanges(n)
498                                 * call for this logger name, not just once - same amplification risk
499                                 * CachedLevelResolver guards against for level properties. Fall back to
500                                 * "nothing allowed to change" and alert exactly once per logger name
501                                 * instead, since the fallback value is itself cached above just like a
502                                 * successful parse would be. validateNow's own Missing = failure
503                                 * semantics are moot here - the lambda above never returns a Missing
504                                 * result to it in the first place.
505                                 */
506                                config().alerts().error(ChangePublisher.class, e);
507                                return Set.of();
508                        }
509                });
510        }
511
512        @Override
513        public CallerType callerType(String loggerName) {
514                return callerTypeCache.computeIfAbsent(loggerName, n -> {
515                        LogProperty.Result<CallerType> result = config().properties()
516                                .findOrNull(LogProperties.CALLER_PREFIX, n, (props, fullKey) -> {
517                                        LogProperty.Result<CallerType> r = props.forKey(fullKey).ofString().map(CallerType::parse);
518                                        return r instanceof LogProperty.Result.Missing ? null : r;
519                                });
520                        if (result == null) {
521                                return CallerType.NONE;
522                        }
523                        try {
524                                return result.validateNow(ChangePublisher.class);
525                        }
526                        catch (LogProperty.ValidationException e) {
527                                /*
528                                 * Same reasoning as allowedChanges()'s catch above: a malformed (or
529                                 * pre-split, e.g. the old "caller" token that used to live in
530                                 * logging.change.<name>) logging.caller.<name> value alerts once and
531                                 * falls back to CallerType.NONE, cached, rather than re-parsing and
532                                 * re-alerting on every call.
533                                 */
534                                config().alerts().error(ChangePublisher.class, e);
535                                return CallerType.NONE;
536                        }
537                });
538        }
539
540}

542enum IgnoreChangePublisher implements ChangePublisher {
543
544        INSTANT;
545
546        @Override
547        public void subscribe(Consumer<? super LogConfig> consumer) {
548        }
549
550        @Override
551        public void publish() {
552
553        }
554
555        @Override
556        public boolean isEnabled(String loggerName) {
557                return false;
558        }
559
560        @Override
561        public Set<ChangeType> allowedChanges(String loggerName) {
562                return Set.of();
563        }
564
565        @Override
566        public CallerType callerType(String loggerName) {
567                return CallerType.NONE;
568        }
569
570}
571
572final class DefaultLogConfig implements LogConfig {
573
574        private final ServiceRegistry registry;
575
576        private final LogProperties properties;
577
578        private final LevelConfig levelResolver;
579
580        private final ChangePublisher changePublisher;
581
582        private final LogOutputRegistry outputRegistry;
583
584        private final LogEncoderRegistry encoderRegistry;
585
586        private final LogPublisherRegistry publisherRegistry;
587
588        private final LogAlerts alerts;
589
590        private final LogMetrics metrics;
591
592        DefaultLogConfig(ServiceRegistry registry, LogProperties properties, LevelConfig levelResolver, LogAlerts alerts,
593                        LogMetrics metrics) {
594                super();
595                this.registry = registry;
596                this.properties = properties;
597                this.levelResolver = levelResolver;
598                this.alerts = alerts;
599                this.metrics = metrics;
600                boolean changeable = properties.forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_CHANGE_PROPERTY)
601                        .ofBoolean()
602                        .or(false)
603                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class);
604                this.changePublisher = changeable ? new DefaultChangePublisher() : IgnoreChangePublisher.INSTANT;
605                applyGlobalAppenderReentrantLockProperty(properties);
606                applyGlobalThreadLocalDisabledProperty(properties);
607                applyGlobalOptimizeProperty(properties);
608                this.outputRegistry = DefaultOutputRegistry.of(registry);
609                this.encoderRegistry = DefaultEncoderRegistry.of();
610                this.publisherRegistry = DefaultPublisherRegistry.of();
611                /*
612                 * addInternalListener, not addListener: a passive in-process counter nobody has
613                 * wired an exporter to does not count as "someone is watching" for
614                 * LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction's purposes - see DefaultLogAlerts's own
615                 * comment on hasExternalListener. alerts is always a DefaultLogAlerts; LogAlerts
616                 * is sealed to permit only that one implementation.
617                 */
618                ((DefaultLogAlerts) this.alerts).addInternalListener(event -> this.metrics.errorCounter(event.loggerName(), 1));
619        }
620
621        /*
622         * Deliberately mutates process-wide static state (AbstractLogAppender's field) rather
623         * than per-instance state - LogProperties#GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY is
624         * a global guarantee by design (see its javadoc), not a per-LogConfig setting.
625         * Last-writer-wins if multiple RainbowGum instances with different values coexist in
626         * one JVM - an accepted tradeoff for a property whose whole point is a process-wide
627         * guarantee independent of any single instance's configuration.
628         */
629        private static void applyGlobalAppenderReentrantLockProperty(LogProperties properties) {
630                AbstractLogAppender.forceReentrantLockAppenders = properties
631                        .forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY)
632                        .ofBoolean()
633                        .or(false)
634                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class);
635        }
636
637        /*
638         * An enum (TRUE/FALSE) rather than .ofBoolean() deliberately, unlike its sibling just
639         * above - a typo'd value here (e.g. "yse") fails loudly through the existing
640         * Property/Result machinery instead of silently resolving to "not disabled", which is
641         * the wrong failure mode for a property whose whole point is a hard, otherwise
642         * easy-to-silently-miss guarantee.
643         */
644        private enum ThreadLocalDisabled {
645
646                TRUE, FALSE;
647
648                static ThreadLocalDisabled parse(String value) {
649                        return ThreadLocalDisabled.valueOf(value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
650                }
651
652        }
653
654        /*
655         * Same last-writer-wins/process-wide-guarantee tradeoff as
656         * applyGlobalAppenderReentrantLockProperty just above - see that method's comment.
657         * rainbowgum-slf4j independently reads this same property key at its own SLF4J
658         * provider initialize() touchpoint to decide whether to disable MDC too - see
659         * LogProperties#GLOBAL_THREADLOCAL_DISABLED_PROPERTY's javadoc for why that is two
660         * independent readers rather than one shared flag.
661         */
662        private static void applyGlobalThreadLocalDisabledProperty(LogProperties properties) {
663                AbstractLogAppender.forceNoThreadLocalAppenders = properties
664                        .forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_THREADLOCAL_DISABLED_PROPERTY)
665                        .ofString()
666                        .map(ThreadLocalDisabled::parse)
667                        .or(ThreadLocalDisabled.FALSE)
668                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class) == ThreadLocalDisabled.TRUE;
669        }
670
671        /*
672         * Same enum-not-boolean reasoning as ThreadLocalDisabled above. Unlike the other two
673         * global properties this one is not a "force/guarantee" downgrade applied after a
674         * type is already resolved - it changes what the *default* resolves to when nothing
675         * more specific (an explicit appenderType(...)/useGetBytes(...) call, or a more
676         * specific property) was set, so it is read into the same kind of process-wide static
677         * flag but consulted at a different point (LogAppender.Builder#build(),
678         * LogEncoder.Builder#build()) - see LogProperties#GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY's javadoc.
679         */
680        private enum GlobalOptimize {
681
682                TRUE, FALSE;
683
684                static GlobalOptimize parse(String value) {
685                        return GlobalOptimize.valueOf(value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
686                }
687
688        }
689
690        private static void applyGlobalOptimizeProperty(LogProperties properties) {
691                AbstractLogAppender.globalOptimizeEnabled = properties.forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY)
692                        .ofString()
693                        .map(GlobalOptimize::parse)
694                        .or(GlobalOptimize.FALSE)
695                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class) == GlobalOptimize.TRUE;
696        }
697
698        class DefaultChangePublisher extends AbstractChangePublisher {
699
700                @Override
701                protected LogConfig config() {
702                        return DefaultLogConfig.this;
703                }
704
705                @Override
706                protected LogConfig reload() {
707                        levelResolver.clear();
708                        return DefaultLogConfig.this;
709                }
710
711        }
712
713        @Override
714        public LogProperties properties() {
715                return properties;
716        }
